name: Universal Planning Networks
title: Universal Planning Networks
summary: Differentiable latent-space planning is trained through an inner trajectory optimizer and transfers goal representations to new robot control problems.

policy.baseModel: Gradient-based latent world-model planning. Convolutional image encoder, latent forward dynamics and unrolled gradient-descent planner.
policy.inputs: Current and goal RGB images; embodiment sensorimotor state for dynamics/planning. Transfer policies may use the learned metric as a shaped reward.
policy.outputs: Planned continuous controls; transfer experiments additionally train RL controllers using the learned latent reward.
policy.trainingData: 20,000 demonstrations each for three-/four-link reachers; manipulation experiment uses 20,000 pokes to learn representations for pushing.
policy.trainingTime: One million minibatch updates, approximately 1.5 days.
policy.trainingMethod: Imitation loss differentiates through trajectory optimization; representation transfers through goal-metric reward to RL policies.
policy.evaluation: MuJoCo reacher and morphology transfer, plus object poking-to-pushing skill transfer; navigation/locomotion experiments are separate.

name: Visual MPC with Retrying
title: Robustness via Retrying: Closed-Loop Robotic Manipulation with Self-Supervised Learning
summary: Video prediction and self-supervised image registration let a robot repeatedly replan toward a visual manipulation goal.

policy.baseModel: Self-supervised visual model predictive control. Action-conditioned video predictor, image-to-image registration model and CEM trajectory optimization.
policy.inputs: Current RGB image and desired goal image with user-designated object pixels; robot control state used by the action-conditioned predictor.
policy.outputs: Cartesian x/y/z displacement and gripper azimuth, with a grasp primitive; replanning maintains visual goal correspondence.
policy.trainingData: 20,000 autonomous pushing trajectories and 15,000 trajectories with gripper control; approximately 160 robot-hours, 150 training objects.
policy.trainingMethod: Self-supervised video and image registration learning on robot interaction data; goal-directed CEM planning with retries at execution.
policy.evaluation: Two Sawyer arms on unseen-object prehensile/nonprehensile relocation; additional MuJoCo L-block pushing experiments.

name: CoRe
title: Imagining Recovery: Inference-Time Counterfactual Realignment for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: A frozen VLA is probed on counterfactually restored observations to choose a minimal physical recovery after task switches or disruptions.
institution: Not reported in accessible author affiliation markup

policy.baseModel: Inference-time counterfactual recovery wrapper. Frozen π0/π0.5, X-VLA, GR00T and OpenVLA variants; calibrated 3D observation synthesis rather than a learned video world model.
policy.inputs: VLA observations/state/language plus a recovery system with depth, object masks/poses, robot kinematics and retained scene geometry. Simulation uses privileged poses/masks; real perception uses Grounding-DINO, SAM2 and shape-specific geometry.
policy.outputs: Recovery object-restoration plan and robot rejoin configuration, followed by resumed frozen-policy actions.
policy.trainingData: Underlying policy demonstrations only; real π0.5 fine-tuning uses 100 clean demonstrations each for pick, place and push.
policy.trainingTime: No recovery-specific training; underlying fine-tuning wall time not reported.
policy.trainingHardware: Real π0.5 fine-tuning: one H200. Physical inference/perception: two RTX 4090 cards; simulation evaluation uses RTX A6000 shards.
policy.controlRate: Real xArm6 control 10 Hz; ten-step policy chunks, eight executed before a query.
policy.trainingMethod: Underlying policies are task-trained offline; recovery uses OOD detection, synthesized counterfactual observations and physical restoration without policy updates.
policy.evaluation: LangSwitch language changes, perturbed LIBERO-Long and physical xArm6 recovery.

name: SILVR
title: Self-Improving Loops for Visual Robotic Planning
summary: Self-collected robot trajectories iteratively improve an in-domain visual planner while a frozen internet video prior supplies broader motion guidance.

policy.baseModel: Self-improving visual planning with inverse dynamics. Small in-domain video diffusion model, frozen AnimateDiff/SparseCtrl prior and inverse dynamics; optional distilled Diffusion Policy.
policy.modelSize: In-domain model: 179.91M (MetaWorld) or 156.58M (real). Internet video model: 2.005B; these are separate components.
policy.inputs: Current RGB, text task prompt and visual plans. Inverse dynamics translates generated futures into control; long-horizon real extension uses Gemini 2.5 skill switching.
policy.outputs: Eight future-frame plans and eight-action controls; optional direct diffusion-policy action output.
policy.trainingData: MetaWorld in-domain initialization uses eight seen tasks with 25 demonstrations/task; each improvement iteration collects 30 new trajectories. Real experiments cover cup pushing and drawer opening.
policy.trainingTime: In-domain initialization: 70,000 MetaWorld or 88,000 Panda steps. Per iteration: 10,000 MetaWorld, 8,000 cup-pushing or 10,000 drawer steps; wall time not reported.
policy.trainingHardware: A single NVIDIA A6000 or RTX 3090.
policy.controlRate: Evaluates open-loop, per-action replanning and intermediate control schedules; a single universal Hz is not reported.
policy.trainingMethod: Inverse probabilistic adaptation combines internet and in-domain visual models; robot interaction updates in-domain video and inverse-dynamics weights.
policy.evaluation: MetaWorld novel tasks and physical Panda cup pushing/drawer opening, with optional language-ordered multi-cup extension.

policy.outputs: Reusable domain programs and closed-loop robot plans for new initial states / goal configurations.
policy.trainingData: No end-to-end policy training is required; generated programs are reused across configurations within a task domain.
policy.trainingHardware: Physical perception / grasp tools run on an RTX 4090 workstation with an AMD Threadripper PRO 5955WX; this is runtime hardware, not a reported model-training cost.
policy.trainingMethod: Frozen VLM program synthesis guided by an explicit shared representation; generated programs cooperate through perception / rendering / relation / planning interfaces.
policy.evaluation: Cube stacking, tangram arrangement and 3D block assembly in simulation and on a Franka Research 3 with Robotiq 2F-85.

release.notes: The original paper is public; code, model and dataset release scopes are verified separately where established. The frozen agent itself has no separately trained method-specific checkpoint; upstream model access has its own terms.

name: HuGo
title: HuGo: LLMs as Whole-Body Policy Code Designers for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
summary: Generates and iteratively refines high-level whole-body policy code over a frozen humanoid controller using numerical rollouts and selected video evidence.
institution: University of California, Berkeley; ShanghaiTech University; Google DeepMind; Nomagic

policy.baseModel: GPT-5.4 code designer / evaluator over frozen rl_isaac or SONIC 3-Point VR whole-body policies.
policy.inputs: Task and robot / interface specifications; high-level code receives numerical state. Refinement uses trajectories, internal code state and ten selected video frames per rollout.
policy.outputs: Closed-loop policy code producing base motion, end-effector targets and torso / pelvis-height commands.
policy.trainingData: No task-specific demonstrations or example policy programs; executed simulation / physical trajectories provide refinement evidence. Low-level policies are pretrained separately.
policy.trainingHardware: IsaacSim experiments use a single NVIDIA L40S GPU; hosted LLM inference is separate.
policy.controlRate: Generated high-level policy code runs at 50 Hz with rl_isaac and 10 Hz with SONIC.
policy.trainingMethod: Frozen LLM and low-level controller weights; feedback-driven code diffs refine the high-level policy, including directly from physical rollouts.
policy.evaluation: Five Unitree G1 simulated tasks, including pushing / lifting, and physical Lift Box / Push Button transfer with fifteen trials per selected policy.

release.notes: Author repository is a placeholder; substantive implementation is not released in its current README. The frozen agent itself has no separately trained method-specific checkpoint; upstream model access has its own terms.

name: DualManip
title: DualManip: Agentic Dynamic Manipulation via Dual-Path Semantic Reasoning and Geometric Adaptation
summary: Separates slow semantic planning from fast learned geometric correspondence updates, adapting grasp contacts to object motion and deformation.
institution: Tsinghua University; Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen); Beijing Institute of Control Engineering

policy.baseModel: GPT-5.6 Terra semantic VLM, Sofar orientation inference, AnyGrasp and a trained shape-adaptive correspondence network; Qwen3.5-2B is a latency-study variant.
policy.modelSize: Local latency-study VLM: 2B; total system size and correspondence-network parameters are not reported.
policy.inputs: Task, live RGB-D point clouds and a pre-scanned object reference template; geometric feasibility checks can request semantic replanning.
policy.outputs: Task-conditioned grasp plan, continuously reconstructed grasp contacts / poses and selective fallback to the semantic agent.
policy.trainingData: One hundred RGB-D observations per object from each camera viewpoint train correspondence learning; reference templates are fixed before evaluation.
policy.trainingHardware: Local perception / control runs on an RTX 3090 workstation; the paper does not separately specify correspondence-training hardware.
policy.controlRate: Mean geometric adaptation latency is 138.7 ms in the reported single-change study; this is not a guaranteed arm-servo frequency.
policy.trainingMethod: Offline correspondence-network training plus frozen semantic models / grasp tools; live geometric adaptation avoids repeated semantic reasoning until feasibility fails.
policy.evaluation: Six real KUKA LBR iiwa tasks under static, single-change and continuous dynamic conditions, including precision assembly; fifteen trials per object / condition / method.

release.notes: The original paper is public; code, model and dataset release scopes are verified separately where established.
